---
title: "Options"
---

There are two sets of settings: the page's, in Quarto, and the relay's, in Apps Script.

## Page settings

These go in the `issue-comments:` block in `_quarto.yml` or a page's front matter. Only `endpoint` is required.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | *(required)* | The Apps Script web app URL, ending in `/exec`. Every site can use the same one. |
| `owner` | the document's first `author`, else "the site owner" | The name readers are told the issue is posted on behalf of. |
| `contact` | none (Quarto warns) | Where readers go to change or remove a comment: a contact page, your GitHub profile, or `mailto:you@example.com`. Only `http`, `https`, `mailto` and relative links are used. |
| `preview` | `true` | Show readers the exact issue before it posts. |
| `passcode` | `false` | Show a passcode box. Set it when the relay has `PASSCODE`. |
| `page-button` | `false` | Also show a fixed "Comment on this page" button, for comments not tied to a passage. |
| `text` | the wording below | Replace any of the wording readers see. |

With the block in `_quarto.yml`, a single page can opt out with `issue-comments: false` in its front matter.

## Wording

Everything readers see can be reworded with `text:`. Give only the keys you want to change; the rest keep their defaults. Quarto warns about a key it doesn't recognise.

```yaml
issue-comments:
  endpoint: https://script.google.com/macros/s/XXXXXXXX/exec
  contact: mailto:jane@example.com
  text:
    heading: Comment on the draft plan
    notice: >-
      This draft is shared with the study team only. Comments are filed as
      GitHub issues for {owner}; to change or remove one, {contact}.
    post: Send to the team
```

A word in braces is filled in where it appears. `{owner}` works in every key.

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `button` | 💬 Comment |
| `page-button` | 💬 Comment on this page |
| `heading` | Leave a comment |
| `preview-heading` | Check before posting |
| `section` | Section: {section} |
| `name-label` | Your name |
| `comment-label` | Comment |
| `passcode-label` | Passcode |
| `notice` | Comments are posted publicly as GitHub issues on behalf of {owner}, together with your name, the highlighted text and a link to this section. You can't edit or delete a comment after posting; to change or remove one, {contact}. Your name is saved in this browser so you don't have to retype it. |
| `contact-link` | contact {owner} *(the text of the `{contact}` link)* |
| `preview-intro` | This is exactly what will be posted publicly on GitHub on behalf of {owner}: |
| `cancel`, `edit`, `close` | Cancel, Edit, Close |
| `preview`, `post` | Preview, Post publicly |
| `posting` | Posting… |
| `thanks` | Thanks! Posted as {issue}. |
| `issue-link` | issue #{number} *(the text of the `{issue}` link)* |

Wording is always shown as plain text, so nothing in it can add HTML to the page. Three things are not set here:

- **The issue itself** (title, "Submitted by", the section link) is written by the relay, so a reader can't change it, and the preview shows it as it will be.
- **Error messages**, such as "That passcode is not correct", come from the relay.
- **The notice should stay true.** If you reword it, keep telling readers that comments are public, who receives them, and how to have one removed.

## Passcode {#passcode}

A passcode keeps commenting to the people you give it to. Set `PASSCODE` in the relay's Script Properties, and `passcode: true` on every site that uses the relay, so readers see the box. One passcode covers all your sites.

Use a long phrase, such as four unrelated words, rather than something memorable. Wrong guesses count against `MAX_PER_HOUR`, so they can't be tried quickly, but that also means a run of guesses can use up a site's allowance for an hour. To change the passcode, change the property; readers aren't asked to remember it between visits.

## Relay settings

These are Script Properties in the Apps Script project (**Project Settings → Script Properties**). A change takes effect on the next comment, with no redeployment.

| Property | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GITHUB_APP_ID` | *(required)* | The App ID from your GitHub App's settings page. |
| `GITHUB_APP_KEY` | *(required)* | The app's private key: the whole `.pem` file. Either format GitHub uses is accepted, with or without line breaks. |
| `GITHUB_OWNER` | none | Your GitHub user name. A page at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/…` sends its comments to `<owner>/<repo>`. |
| `REPO_MAP` | none | Sites at any other address, as JSON from address to repository. See below. |
| `PASSCODE` | none | The passcode readers must enter. See [Passcode](#passcode). |
| `LABEL` | `reader-comment` | The label put on every comment's issue, so you can filter them. |
| `MAX_PER_HOUR` | `20` | The most comments accepted for one repository in any 60 minutes. Each repository has its own count. |

Whichever way a page is matched, a repository only receives comments if the app is installed on it.

### `REPO_MAP`

`REPO_MAP` covers a site on its own domain, a user site (`https://<owner>.github.io/` itself), a site whose comments should go to a different repository, and `quarto preview`:

```json
{
  "https://plan.example.org/": "VagishHemmige/USRDS",
  "https://vagishhemmige.github.io/HIV-SLK/": "VagishHemmige/HIV-SLK-comments",
  "http://localhost:4200/": "VagishHemmige/test-comments"
}
```

Each address is the start of the page addresses it covers. When several match, the longest wins, and a match here takes priority over the `GITHUB_OWNER` rule. Plain `http` is accepted only for `localhost`, for previews. `quarto preview` can pick a different port each time, so give it one with `--port 4200`.

## Maintenance

**The private key.** It doesn't expire. To replace it, generate a new one on the app's page, paste it into `GITHUB_APP_KEY`, and delete the old key on the app's page. No redeployment is needed.

**Adding a site.** Install the app on its repository, and give the site the same `endpoint`. See [Adding another site](installation.qmd#adding-another-site).

**Updating the script.** After changing `Code.gs`, use **Deploy → Manage deployments → Edit → Version: New version**. That keeps the same `/exec` URL. **New deployment** gives a new URL, which every page using the relay would then need.

**Changing the issue format.** The page previews the issue itself, so the format is written twice: `buildIssue_` in `Code.gs`, and `issueTitle` and `fillPreview` in `issue-comments.js`. Change both together. See [How it works](how-it-works.qmd#two-copies-of-the-issue-format).
